# Lenz 0.0.15 beta

This release improves Lenz Code branch navigation and fixes editor and window-close issues.

- Reuse branch metadata while refreshing, avoiding status scans of every worktree before choices appear. Group local branches, remote branches, tags and worktrees in GUI and TUI.
- Restore Code native Quit/Command-Q handling and show close questions with transient pickers or running terminals. Prevent a close/resize repaint loop and cancel Git-status work during teardown.
- Fix scratch input focus, add GUI scratch filtering, clarify editable-source origin notices, and report exhausted scratch numbering safely.
- Reject disk-check replies based on an older Save baseline, preserving detection of actual external edits.

## Validation

The merged fixes pass the full local Linux gate, native GUI/TUI light/dark/narrow replays and sustained normal-release workloads. Cached usable branch choices measure **20.635 → 1.407 ms** with 1,000 generated refs and three worktrees. The first frame is about **0.6 ms** slower and contains cached choices; a roughly **0.04 ms** upward TUI key-feedback tendency was explicitly accepted. See the [audit report](../research/code-branch-picker-audit.md) for identities, raw evidence, rejected experiments and limits.

Native AppKit/macOS interaction and physical-display behavior remain unverified. Native package build/signature and CLI checks are separate from interactive validation. macOS packages are ad-hoc signed.

Keep all five executables together. Verify the matching `.sha256` sidecar before installation.

[Changes since 0.0.14](https://github.com/aantoniadis/lenz/compare/v0.0.14...v0.0.15).
